inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2-2026 10-Q diluted weighted average 69.403M (cover-page basic 69.354M at 2026-07-29). Held FLAT because SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows; charging dilution as well would double-count. Q1-2026 included a $300M repurchase (possibly an ASR whose final share delivery is still to settle -- any residual delivery would lower the count modestly and is not credited here).
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL companyfacts (10-K FY2025, 10-Q Q2-2026): TTM-Jun-2026 ShareBasedCompensation cash-flow add-back 77.9 (FY25 62.7 - H1-25 25.7 + H1-26 40.9) plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation 19.2 (25.9 - 22.9 + 16.2). Insulet publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: Actual financing outflow: FY2025 $59.6M, H1-2026 $300.0M (all in Q1-2026). Insulet is a repurchaser, so the flat count is being funded; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.0-1.1 x 5.0% ERP gives cost of equity ~9.5%; ~10% debt weight (term loan, ~$0.95B against ~$9B market cap) at ~6.5% pre-tax pulls WACC to ~9.0%. Single WACC across scenarios -- single-platform and Type 2 retention risk is charged through the 25% bear weight, not a premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost (liability $51.9M at FY25) sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside EBITDA; the $7.4M finance lease is inside total_debt. One treatment, no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct 0).
inputs.interest_income_note: Not deducted: Insulet is NET DEBT ($948.4M term loan + finance lease vs $534.9M cash), so there is no surplus cash pile being double-counted. The engine builds unlevered flows from EBITDA, so interest income (TTM $22.9M) and interest expense (TTM ~$58.8M) are both outside the projected flows and net debt is deducted once in the bridge.
inputs.fy0_note: fy0 is the twelve months to 30 June 2026 (FY25 - H1-25 + H1-26) so the base revenue matches the 30 June 2026 balance sheet; year 1 = Jul-26..Jun-27. TTM revenue 3,053.4; TTM GAAP EBITDA 615.0 + SBC 77.9 = 692.9 pre-SBC EBITDA (22.7%); D&A 99.3 (3.25%); capex 217.5 (7.1%); cash tax FY25 $38.5M on $339.5M pretax (~11%, NOL/credit shelter).
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF = reported TTM FCF 293.7 (OCF 511.2 - capex 217.5) - SBC incl. withholding taxes 97.1 - interest income 0 = 196.6. Reported TTM FCF is depressed by an H1-26 inventory build (+$34.9M) and is post-interest; the unlevered component build reaches a ~9-10% owner-FCF margin in year 1.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company'). Insulet is a US medtech operating company -- razor-and-blade Omnipod pods through the pharmacy channel -- with no bank/REIT/holdco features; no MEMORY.md entry existed, so this is the first model decision for the ticker. US filer reporting and quoting USD; non-US adaptations not needed. Data: Metrics.csv lacks cash for 2022 onward, so cash/debt/shares/SBC/withholding/capex were read directly from SEC XBRL companyfacts (CIK 1145197) at the Q2-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-05). Guidance context: Q2-26 cut US Omnipod FY26 growth to 17-19% (from 20-22%) on Type 2 first-90-day attrition, raised International to 30-32% cc, raised adj. EPS growth to >=30%, preliminary 2027 'mid-teens exit growth' vs the Nov-2025 Investor Day ~20% framework; ~100bps/yr adj. operating-margin expansion maintained. Price sits near the 52-week low after a ~20% post-print fall.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance_adjusted: FY2027 preliminary 'mid-teens exit growth' (Q2-26 release)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 47.1% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr 27.5%: FY22 equity was depressed by convertible-note accounting and FY24 net income (418.3 vs operating income 308.9) includes a large tax benefit. EPS CAGRs are meaningless off near-zero FY20/FY22 bases (0.11, 0.07).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes; interest income not deducted as the company is net debt): FY20 -110.7, FY21 -242.6, FY22 -61.6, FY23 8.5, FY24 228.4, FY25 289.1 -- negative at both 3yr and 5yr start points, so FCF CAGRs are undefined. All historical CAGRs describe a ramp from breakeven and pre-date the Q2-26 guidance cut; the selected 15% is the forward guided exit rate, not a trailing figure.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26..Jun-27) 16%: H2-26 ~+16.5% implied by the cut FY26 guide against a +28% H1, then the guided mid-teens 2027 exit with no credit for Type 2 retention fixes. Decelerates ~1pp/yr to 6% by year 10 as US AID penetration of Type 1 matures; International (30%+ today) carries the mix.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA 22.7% TTM; +~90bps/yr for five years (slightly under the ~100bps adj. operating-margin framework) to a mature 29%, below Dexcom-type device peers given CGM partner dependency and rising competition.
base.capex_rationale: Capex 7.1% TTM is elevated by manufacturing capacity (Malaysia/Massachusetts); tapers to 4.5% as the build-out completes, with D&A rising toward it.
base.tax_rationale: FY25 cash tax ~11% of pretax on NOL/credit shelter; ramps to a 22% normal US federal+state/foreign blend by year 6.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer with receivables and inventory exceeding payables: growth consumes ~8% of incremental revenue (negative capture).

scenario_narratives.base: Management's reset is roughly right. The Type 2 first-90-day attrition is real but contained: US Omnipod grows mid-teens in 2027 and slows toward high single digits as Type 1 AID penetration matures, while International (Middle East, Spain and deeper European share) keeps growing faster and lifts the mix. Omnipod 6 (2027) holds share against Tandem Mobi, Medtronic 780G and Beta Bionics but does not re-accelerate the business. The pharmacy-channel model keeps pricing stable. Adjusted operating margin expands a bit under the ~100bps/yr framework, reaching a mature ~29% pre-SBC EBITDA margin. Revenue compounds ~10.6% a year over ten years.
scenario_narratives.bull: The new onboarding and patient-selection programmes fix Type 2 retention during 2027. Omnipod 6 and the purpose-built Type 2 fully closed-loop system (2028) open the much larger, mostly pump-naive insulin-dependent Type 2 population. Growth comes back to the high teens, near the Investor Day ~20% framework, and International stays above 25% for several years. The pharmacy-channel cost advantage means tubed-pump competitors cannot match the ~$1/day access, and scale in pod manufacturing takes pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 32%, close to Dexcom-type device economics.
scenario_narratives.bear: Type 2 attrition is structural: many pump-naive Type 2 patients do not stay on wearable AID, and GLP-1 adoption shrinks the insulin-dependent Type 2 pool. That leaves Insulet competing for a maturing Type 1 base against Tandem, Medtronic and Beta Bionics, with payers using volume contracts to press on pod pricing. Growth falls to high single digits by 2028. Customer-acquisition spend and price concessions absorb the manufacturing gains, so margin expansion stalls near 25%. CGM-partner dependency (Dexcom/Abbott) caps differentiation, and guidance credibility stays impaired, so a lower 14x exit multiple applies.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the business depends on one platform and the Type 2 retention problem is still unquantified, with management assuming no fix in the 2027 outlook. Base held at 50% because the guided mid-teens 2027 exit is the best evidence available. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent wins (a retention fix, Omnipod 6 on time, the 2028 Type 2 closed-loop clearance, and no erosion of pharmacy-channel pricing).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on a 10-year component build from TTM June 2026. SBC and the cash taxes withheld on equity awards are both charged as costs, and the share count is held flat at the fully diluted 69.4M. Net debt of $413.5M at 30 June 2026 is deducted once. The 2027 driver year follows the post-cut guidance ('mid-teens exit', no credit for retention fixes), not the November 2025 Investor Day ~20% framework. Margin expansion is assumed slightly below the company's ~100bps/yr target.
key_risks_to_valuation: Type 2 retention: whether first-90-day attrition is fixable decides between base and bear growth from 2028
Competition from Tandem Mobi, Medtronic and Beta Bionics, and payer pricing pressure on pods
Pipeline timing: Omnipod 6 (2027) and the Type 2 closed-loop system (2028) both need regulatory clearance
Terminal value carries most of the value at a 9% WACC; each 1pp of WACC moves base value materially (see sensitivity)
GLP-1 adoption shrinking the insulin-dependent Type 2 population
